name: Spin-coat positive photoresist on a 100 mm Si wafer
description: A six-step closed-world protocol for spin-coating S1813 positive photoresist onto a 100 mm (4 in) silicon wafer at 4000 rpm for 30 s, followed by a 90 s soft-bake at 115 °C. Canonical academic-cleanroom workflow used as the OpenLabOS reference protocol — exercises object_on_surface, component_added, action_performed, and measurement_in_range criteria, with two real safety notes (PGMEA solvent flammability, hot-plate burn risk).

steps.title: Load the wafer onto the spin-coater chuck
steps.instruction: Using wafer tweezers, place a clean 100 mm silicon wafer flat-side down, centred on the spin-coater chuck. The wafer flat should align with the reference notch on the chuck.

success_criteria.description: wafer rests centred on the chuck, flat side down

failure_modes.description: no wafer visible on the chuck
wafer off-centre — will throw off-axis at speed

safety_notes: Handle wafers only with tweezers — finger oils contaminate the surface and degrade resist adhesion.

steps.title: Engage the chuck vacuum
steps.instruction: Toggle the vacuum-on switch on the spin-coater. Confirm the wafer is locked to the chuck by gently nudging the edge with the tweezers — the wafer should not move.

success_criteria.description: vacuum-on indicator (LED or gauge) reads engaged

failure_modes.description: vacuum gauge reads insufficient draw — wafer not seated, will fly at speed

steps.title: Dispense 3 mL of S1813 photoresist onto wafer centre
steps.instruction: Using a clean disposable transfer pipette, dispense roughly 3 mL of S1813 resist as a continuous puddle onto the wafer centre. Avoid bubbles; do not let the pipette tip contact the surface.

success_criteria.description: amber resist puddle visible at wafer centre, covering ~30 mm radius

failure_modes.description: resist visibly off the wafer onto the chuck or bowl
puddle has visible bubbles — will print as voids

safety_notes: S1813 contains PGMEA — flammable, vapours irritate eyes and respiratory tract. Work inside the fume hood with the sash low.
Wear nitrile gloves and safety glasses; double-glove if dispensing >5 mL.

steps.title: Close the spin-coater bowl lid
steps.instruction: Lower the spin-coater bowl lid until it seats. The interlock should latch and the run-enable indicator should illuminate.

success_criteria.description: lid seated on the bowl rim, interlock LED lit

failure_modes.description: spin engaged without the lid latched — chemical spray hazard

safety_notes: Never bypass the lid interlock. A 4000 rpm spin without the lid will spray resist throughout the hood.

steps.title: Run the spin program: 4000 rpm for 30 s
steps.instruction: Press start. Verify the recipe shows 500 rpm spread for 5 s, then 4000 rpm spin for 30 s, then ramp-down. Wait for the cycle to complete and the chuck to stop.

success_criteria.description: spin cycle runs to completion; tachometer reaches setpoint and ramps down
tachometer holds 4000 ± 50 rpm during the main spin

failure_modes.description: speed setpoint differed from 4000 rpm — film thickness off-target
audible imbalance or vibration — wafer may have lifted

steps.title: Soft-bake on hotplate at 115 °C for 90 s
steps.instruction: Transfer the coated wafer with tweezers onto the calibrated hotplate. The hotplate setpoint must read 115 °C and be at temperature. Time the bake to 90 s, then move the wafer to a cooling chuck.

success_criteria.description: wafer flat on hotplate surface during bake

failure_modes.description: hotplate not at temperature — under-bake leaves residual solvent, over-bake hardens resist beyond developable
wafer placed on cold hotplate that was being warmed up — uneven bake

safety_notes: Hotplate surface and tweezers tip are hot — burn risk. Use silicone-tipped tweezers if available.
Do not bend over a 115 °C hotplate face-down; convective vapours include residual PGMEA.
